ak-agentkit.tagline: Task router: classifies work and chains the shortest skill workflow.
ak-agentkit.summary: ak:agentkit classifies a task by workflow class, size, risk, and domain count, then routes it to one installed owner skill. It returns a routing record: main skill, chain, subagent timing, and verification level.
howItWorks: Named skills or one obvious domain go straight to the owner; plain conversation needs no workflow.
Ambiguous work is matched only against the live installed catalog, never a remembered list.
Picks one class (e.g. build-feature, fix-defect, review-audit) plus size, risk, and domain modifiers.
Chains run understand → decide → execute → verify → deliver; higher risk adds verify and review.
Delegates to subagents per references/subagent-timing.md; failed links detour, never advance.
useWhen: Starting multi-step or multi-domain work without knowing which skill goes first.
Ordering several skills into one workflow, e.g. research → plan → cook → review.
Deciding when to spawn subagents like tester, code-reviewer, or kongming.
avoidWhen: You already know the skill: call it directly, e.g. /ak:fix.
Plain Q&A or explanation: use /ak:ask or /ak:explain.
Listing skills or commands: use /ak:help.

params.name: [task to route]
params.desc: Task description to route; returns a route to the installed owner skill. No flags.

examples.cmd: /ak:agentkit add Google sign-in to the Next.js app, update docs, and write e2e tests
examples.note: Multi-domain (auth, frontend, docs, test): one main owner plus one execute sub-link per domain, in dependency order.

examples.cmd: /ak:agentkit CI is red after a dependency upgrade
examples.note: fix-defect class: routes straight to /ak:fix; the debugger role joins only after two failed fixes.

examples.cmd: /ak:agentkit I want to understand why this service is slow, then decide whether to refactor
examples.note: investigate-explain first with no change link; brainstorm/plan only if it becomes delivery.

tips: The router routes and stops; it does not repeat gates the owner skill runs.
On a tie between classes, it picks the shorter route and records why.
Pass artifact paths between chain links instead of prose summaries.
artifacts: Routing record in the conversation (class, modifiers, chain, reason)
Subagent reports in plans/reports/ when the project uses that convention

ak-help.tagline: AgentKit help index: installed skills, commands, and workflows.
ak-help.summary: ak:help answers how to use ak, which skills exist, and which workflow to run. It reads the live installed catalog and `ak --help`, never remembered lists.
howItWorks: Reads the installed-skill catalog, or only the frontmatter of SKILL.md files in skill roots.
Points to the most specific installed skill and says plainly when one is missing.
For commands, reads `ak --help` or the command's own help at question time.
Resolves the real owner when project skills shadow user skills.
useWhen: You are new to AgentKit and want to see available skills.
You need `ak` CLI syntax, e.g. `ak plan` or `ak config`.
You want workflow suggestions before running anything.
avoidWhen: Automatic classification and skill chaining: use /ak:agentkit.
A skill that is not installed: use /ak:find-skills.
Installing or removing kits: use /ak:ak.

params.name: [topic|skill|command]
params.desc: Optional topic, skill, or command; empty opens the general index.

examples.note: Opens the general index of installed skill groups.
Answers about ak:plan or `ak plan` from the current SKILL.md and `ak plan --help`.

examples.cmd: /ak:help workflow for fixing a CI bug
examples.note: Points to the most specific installed skill, usually /ak:fix.

tips: Answers reflect current installs; ask again after changing kits.
Missing skills are reported, not faked.
Narrow questions cost far fewer tokens than the full catalog.

ak-coding-level.tagline: Set your coding experience level (0-5) to tune explanation depth.
ak-coding-level.summary: ak:coding-level sets explanation depth from 0 (ELI5) to 5 (God Mode, default). It changes wording and examples, never scope, correctness, tests, or security.
howItWorks: Applies the level immediately to explanations, vocabulary, and examples.
Persists via `ak config prefs` when supported, then re-checks the resolved `codingLevel`.
Without persistence support, applies to this session only and says so.
In Claude Code you can also pick a coding-level-N Output style in `/config`.
useWhen: A beginner wants metaphors and step-by-step answers (level 0 or 1).
A tech lead wants answers on risk and business impact (level 4).
Returning to the default efficient mode (level 5).
avoidWhen: One simple explanation: use /ak:explain --eli5.
Rephrasing the last answer: use /ak:bro.
Cutting features or tests: use a skill's --yagni flag instead.

params.desc: 0 ELI5, 1 Junior, 2 Mid-Level, 3 Senior (trade-offs), 4 Tech Lead (risk, strategy), 5 God Mode (expert, default).

examples.note: Non-programmer: everyday metaphors, every term defined.
Tech lead: focus on risk assessment and business impact.
Back to default: short, efficient answers.

tips: A lower level never means less code, tests, or security.
Confirm persistence with `ak config prefs resolve --json`.
Lower levels use more tokens; reset to 5 when done.

ak-ask.tagline: One-shot architecture advice: analyze, compare, recommend. No code.
ak-ask.summary: ak:ask answers technical and architecture questions as a senior architect, with blunt analysis and next steps. It never implements and does not interview you like ak:advise.
howItWorks: Reads repo instructions and docs, then checks their claims against source and config.
Scouts with ak:scout when context is missing.
Applies relevant lenses: systems design, technology strategy, scalability, and risk.
States when the recommendation stops holding; small questions may get one paragraph.
useWhen: Choosing between options, e.g. Postgres vs MongoDB, for this project.
Getting a quick opinion on scalability, reliability, or risk.
You want one analytical answer without back-and-forth.
avoidWhen: A vague idea that needs questioning: use /ak:advise.
Locking an outcome contract before delivery: use /ak:brainstorm.
Deep external research with citations: use /ak:research.

params.name: [technical-question]
params.desc: Technical question or architecture challenge.

params.name: --yagni
params.desc: Challenges and cuts scope not needed for the outcome; default covers the full scope.

examples.cmd: /ak:ask Should this service use a queue (RabbitMQ) or a cron job for bulk email?
examples.note: Compares options against the current codebase.

examples.cmd: /ak:ask Can the current multi-tenant architecture handle 10x tenants?
examples.note: Assesses scalability and risk, including when the advice stops holding.

examples.cmd: /ak:ask Design RBAC permissions for the admin panel --yagni
examples.note: Asks for a minimal design with unneeded scope cut.

tips: User-invoked only; the agent never triggers it on its own.
Specific questions get evidence-based answers; vague ones trigger costly scouting.
It writes no files; move to /ak:plan once you have a recommendation.

ak-advise.tagline: Interview one question at a time, then give honest, evidence-based advice.
ak-advise.summary: ak:advise interviews you about a raw idea, problem, or URL, confirms a reframing, then gives blunt advice with a checklist and success metrics. It advises only and edits nothing beyond its own reports.
howItWorks: Reads the input (GitHub URLs via gh) and scouts relevant source when the topic touches the project.
Interview is a hard gate: exactly one question per turn, usually 4-8 total.
Confirms Problem, Requirements, Goals, Non-goals, Constraints before any advice.
Advice covers verdict, do/don't, better options, path, benefits, trade-offs, checklist, and metrics.
Writes a report; output flags spawn subagents for HTML, Markdown, wiki, or GitHub delivery.
useWhen: You have a raw idea and want it challenged before planning.
You want an honest second opinion on a plan or design.
You want advice posted back to a GitHub issue or PR (--github).
avoidWhen: One analytical answer without an interview: use /ak:ask.
Comparing options and locking a contract for plan/cook: use /ak:brainstorm.
Headless runs with no one to answer: use /ak:brainstorm --ask.

params.name: [prompt-or-url]
params.desc: Idea or problem text, or a URL (GitHub issue/PR, spec, doc). GitHub URLs are kept for --github.

params.name: --html
params.desc: Adds a self-contained HTML report built by ui-ux-designer.

params.name: --md
params.desc: Adds a standalone Markdown report via docs-manager.

params.name: --wiki
params.desc: Uploads the report to AgentWiki, private by default; skipped if unavailable.

params.name: --github
params.desc: Comments the advice on the input issue/PR, or opens a new issue.

params.name: --agent
params.desc: Runs the workflow in the `advisor` subagent while the main session relays questions. Claude Code only; excludes --ultra.

params.name: --ultra
params.desc: Best-of-5: one interview, 5 advice candidates, kongming picks the winner. Conflicts with --agent.

params.name: --yagni
params.desc: Cuts unneeded scope; by default wrong scope is raised as a trade-off.

params.name: --no-antv
params.desc: Disables AntV KPI tiles in --html output.

params.name: --no-diagram-design
params.desc: Disables diagram-design visuals in --html output.

params.name: --no-editorial-visuals
params.desc: Disables all editorial visuals; highest precedence.

examples.cmd: /ak:advise I want to rewrite the whole backend in Rust
examples.note: Big idea: challenge reasons, alternatives, and cost before deciding.
Analyzes the issue, interviews, then comments the advice on it.

examples.cmd: /ak:advise Choose a caching strategy for the API --ultra --yagni
examples.note: Load-bearing decision: 5 independent candidates, best one picked, minimal scope.

tips: Concrete answers (numbers, constraints) converge faster; "make it better" is not a requirement.
You keep the final decision; overrides are recorded as trade-offs.
--ultra costs several times more; use it only for important decisions.
artifacts: Standard advise report in the reports folder

ak-brainstorm.tagline: Turn unclear intent into a delivery contract and compare options.
ak-brainstorm.summary: ak:brainstorm is the opening gate for multi-step delivery: it records Outcome, Constraints, Non-goals, and Acceptance criteria. For bugs it requires a proven root cause, then hands off to ak:plan → ak:cook or ak:fix.
howItWorks: Reuses an accepted contract or plan; non-delivery requests get a direct answer.
Asks only when an answer changes outcome or safety; --ask runs one round of up to 4 decisions.
Bugs: frame expected behavior, scout, prove root cause, then compare cause-aligned fixes.
Presents at most 3 options and recommends the smallest one meeting the contract.
Hands off contract and direction to plan; --yagni and --advice pass downstream, --ask never does.
useWhen: A multi-step feature lacks recorded outcome, constraints, or acceptance criteria.
Several viable implementations need comparison before planning.
A diagnosed bug has multiple possible fixes.
avoidWhen: Simple questions: answer directly or use /ak:ask.
An accepted plan exists: run /ak:cook <plan-path>.
An undiagnosed bug: use /ak:debug or /ak:fix first.

params.name: [topic or problem]
params.desc: Topic, request, or problem to clarify.

params.name: --ask
params.desc: One question round of up to 4 decisions with recommended options. Headless applies reversible defaults. Never passed downstream.

params.name: --advice
params.desc: kongming supervises each phase and high-risk decisions; passed to plan, cook, and fix.

params.name: --html
params.desc: Writes a self-contained brainstorm.html with options, diagram, and UI mockups for UI topics.

params.name: --report
params.desc: Saves a Markdown report brainstorm-{YYMMDD-HHmm}-{slug}.md in the plan or plans/reports/ folder.

params.name: --ultra
params.desc: Best-of-5: 5 read-only candidates; a verifier picks one or rejects all.

params.name: --yagni
params.desc: Cuts scope not needed for the outcome; passed to every downstream skill.

params.name: --no-antv
params.desc: Disables AntV KPI tiles in brainstorm.html.

params.name: --no-diagram-design
params.desc: Uses a plain table instead of the Quadrant comparison in brainstorm.html.

params.name: --no-editorial-visuals
params.desc: Disables all editorial visuals in brainstorm.html.

examples.cmd: /ak:brainstorm Add realtime notifications to the dashboard
examples.note: New feature: lock the contract, compare WebSocket vs SSE vs polling, then /ak:plan.

examples.cmd: /ak:brainstorm Move uploads to S3 presigned URLs --ask --report
examples.note: Several open decisions: one question round with recommendations and a saved report.
UI topic: HTML brief with annotated mockup and workflow diagram.

tips: Clear requests get a four-field summary and move on without questions.
--ultra costs several times more; use it only when results are verifiable.
Pasted secrets become [REDACTED] and you are told to rotate them.

ak-plan.tagline: Create, validate, and red-team implementation plans with executable phases.
ak-plan.summary: ak:plan writes plans/<timestamp>-<slug>/ with a short plan.md index and phase-NN-<name>.md files. It picks a depth mode, runs red-team and validation gates, and hands off to ak:cook; it writes no code.
howItWorks: Picks one mode (flag or auto-detect); two mode flags hard-stop. debate and ultra are opt-in only.
Deeper modes spawn up to 2 researchers and scout before the planner drafts.
Red-team gate: 2-4 adversarial code-reviewers; findings without file:line are dropped; you approve fixes.
Validation gate checks claims against code and writes `## Validation Log`; a sweep checks consistency.
Hands off `/ak:cook {plan-dir}/plan.md`, then runs /ak:journal unless skipped.
useWhen: Work needs phases, architecture decisions, or file ownership before coding.
Parallel agents need separate file boundaries (--parallel).
Validating or red-teaming an existing plan before cooking.
avoidWhen: Small, clear change: use /ak:cook --fast or /ak:fix.
Outcome is still vague: run /ak:brainstorm first.
Issue to validated plan in one command: use /ak:issue-to-plan.

params.name: [task]
params.desc: Task to plan, or an issue or brainstorm output.

params.name: --fast
params.desc: No research; planner writes directly. Reduces depth, never scope.

params.name: --hard
params.desc: Researchers, scout, planner, red-team, validate, task hydration.

params.name: --deep
params.desc: For large overhauls: details Phase 1, outlines the rest; later phases scout during cook.

params.name: --parallel
params.desc: Parallel phases with strict file ownership, for `/ak:cook --parallel`.

params.name: --two
params.desc: Researches 2 architectures with a trade-off matrix, then plans the chosen one.

params.name: --debate
params.desc: Opt-in: 3 parallel planners on shared evidence; the orchestrator merges one plan.

params.name: --ultra
params.desc: Opt-in best-of-5: kongming scores 5 blind drafts and keeps the winner intact. Expensive.

params.name: --auto
params.desc: Explicit auto-detect mode (unlike /ak:cook --auto); conflicts with other mode flags.

params.name: --tdd
params.desc: Requires test-first design and verify commands in every phase.

params.name: --no-tasks
params.desc: Skips hydrating phases into tasks (default hydrates at 3+ phases).

params.name: --html
params.desc: Outputs an interactive plan.html as the main deliverable; plan.md becomes an index.

params.name: --github
params.desc: Creates or updates a `Plan: {plan-title}` GitHub issue labeled `ready to review`.

params.name: --wiki
params.desc: Uploads the reviewed plan to AgentWiki, private by default.

params.name: --advice
params.desc: kongming supervision plus a handover plan with mechanical verify steps for weaker executors.

params.name: --yagni
params.desc: Challenges and removes unneeded scope; default is HOLD SCOPE.

params.name: --skip-journal
params.desc: Skips the automatic /ak:journal step; overrides journal.auto.

params.name: --no-antv
params.desc: Disables AntV visuals in plan.html.

params.name: --no-diagram-design
params.desc: Disables diagram-design visuals in plan.html.

params.name: --no-editorial-visuals
params.desc: Disables all editorial visuals in plan.html.

params.name: validate <path>
params.desc: Checks paths and symbols against code, asks up to 4 key questions, writes `## Validation Log`. Fix failures before cooking.

params.name: red-team <path>
params.desc: 2-4 adversarial reviewers, max 15 findings with file:line; you approve each; adds `## Red Team Review`.

params.name: archive [slug]
params.desc: Marks finished plans archived in the index, optionally journaling; never deletes or moves files.

examples.note: Lets the skill auto-detect the mode from complexity.
New domain: research, red-team, validate, and test-first.
Validates an existing plan before cooking.

tips: Plan files are the source of truth; `ak plan reindex` rebuilds the index.
After validate, `/clear` and run `/ak:cook <absolute-path>/plan.md`.
--fast reduces depth, not features; use --yagni to cut scope.
artifacts: `## Validation Log` and `## Red Team Review` in plan.md

ak-preview.tagline: View files in a clean reader, or generate visuals, slides, and diagrams.
ak-preview.summary: ak:preview opens Markdown in a browser reader, or generates explanations, slides, and diagrams as Markdown or self-contained HTML. HTML-only modes add visual diff review, plan review, and project recap.
howItWorks: No arguments: asks which action to run.
View mode runs a background reader server and reports local and network URLs.
Generation saves to {plan_dir}/visuals/ or plans/visuals/{topic-slug}.md or .html.
--diagram self-reviews the render and re-renders until clean.
HTML output uses ak:frontend-design, needs a light/dark toggle, and passes a quality checklist.
useWhen: Reading a long plan, report, or RFC in the browser.
Explaining a flow visually or making quick slides.
Reviewing a PR visually (--html --diff) or catching up on a project (--html --recap).
avoidWhen: Grounded explanation of a concept or error: use /ak:explain.
Publication-grade diagrams: use /ak:tech-graph or /ak:diagram.
A showcase or demo page: use /ak:show-off.

params.name: [path]
params.desc: File or folder to view; missing paths trigger a question.

params.name: --html
params.desc: One self-contained HTML file; works with --explain, --slides, --diagram, not --ascii.

params.name: --explain
params.desc: Visual explanation: overview, ASCII view, Mermaid flow, key concepts, code example.

params.name: --slides
params.desc: Slide deck, one concept per slide.

params.name: --diagram
params.desc: Focused ASCII + Mermaid diagram with self-review; HTML adds zoom.

params.name: --ascii
params.desc: Terminal-friendly ASCII box diagram; Markdown only.

params.name: --diff
params.desc: HTML-only visual review of a branch, commit, PR (needs gh), or range; default vs main.

params.name: --plan-review
params.desc: HTML-only comparison of a plan with the code: blast radius, risks, gaps.

params.name: --recap
params.desc: HTML-only project snapshot for a timeframe (default 2w); needs git history.

params.name: --stop
params.desc: Stops the running preview server.

params.name: [topic]
params.desc: Topic for generation flags; slugged for the filename. Only the first generation flag applies.

params.name: --no-antv
params.desc: Disables AntV visuals in HTML output.

params.name: --no-diagram-design
params.desc: Disables diagram-design visuals, falling back to Mermaid/Chart.js.

params.name: --no-editorial-visuals
params.desc: Disables all editorial visuals; highest precedence.

examples.note: Reads a plan in the browser novel-reader.
Markdown visual explanation with ASCII + Mermaid.
Visual review of PR #142 (needs gh).

tips: Run `/ak:preview --stop` when done; a running server is reused.
Same-named outputs are overwritten; change the topic to keep old versions.
HTML output loads CDNs; use /ak:explain --html for fully offline files.
artifacts: {plan_dir}/visuals/{topic-slug}.md or .html when a plan is active
Background preview server in view mode

ak-cook.tagline: Implement features, plans, and fixes: implement, verify, review, finalize.
ak-cook.summary: ak:cook is the main implementation skill: it takes a task or plan path and delivers the full authorized scope through verification and review. It then syncs the plan, updates affected docs, and writes a journal.
howItWorks: Picks mode from flags, a plan path, keywords, or feature count; default runs without pauses.
Checks the plan against current source and follows existing helpers and contracts.
Spawns code-simplifier when the diff exceeds thresholds (default 400 LOC / 8 files).
Verifies narrowest check first; never weakens or fakes checks; risky changes get tester and code-reviewer.
Syncs plan checkboxes, updates docs, commits only with permission, then runs /ak:journal.
useWhen: Executing an accepted plan: `/ak:cook plans/.../plan.md`.
Building a clear feature with tests and review, without a long plan.
A refactor needs a test safety net first (--tdd).
avoidWhen: Vague requirements: run /ak:brainstorm then /ak:plan.
A specific bug or red CI: use /ak:fix.
Branch is done and needs a PR: use /ak:ship.

params.name: [task|plan-path]
params.desc: Task in plain language, or a path to plan.md / phase-*.md, which triggers plan execution.

params.name: --interactive
params.desc: Pauses for approval after research, plan, implement, and test. The only mode with human gates.

params.name: --fast
params.desc: Skips research: short plan, implement, verify. Does not skip tests.

params.name: --parallel
params.desc: Delegates file-owned independent work to fullstack-developer subagents.

params.name: --auto
params.desc: Runs all authorized phases without pauses. Default when no flag applies.

params.name: --no-test
params.desc: Skips running tests and reports the gap; other checks still run.

params.name: --tdd
params.desc: Writes tests for current behavior before each refactor phase; old tests must still pass.

params.name: --advice
params.desc: kongming supervises each phase and every failed verify; passed to ship.

params.name: --yagni
params.desc: Cuts unneeded scope; default delivers the full requested scope.

params.name: --skip-journal
params.desc: Skips the final /ak:journal; other finalize steps still run.

examples.note: Executes a validated plan (code mode).

examples.cmd: /ak:cook add a CSV export button to the orders table --fast
examples.note: Small, clear feature with no research.
Independent features delegated in parallel.

tips: After `/clear`, pass the absolute plan.md path.
--parallel is safe only when phases touch different files.
Finalize never implies commit or push permission.
artifacts: Short plan or phase files when coordination is needed
Checkbox and status updates in plan.md and phase-*.md

ak-vibe.tagline: One command from GitHub issue or request to reviewed PR.
ak-vibe.summary: ak:vibe runs the full loop: worktree, TDD plan with gates, cook or fix, code review, ship, PR review, and optional merge with CI watch. It never bypasses gates, tests, review blockers, or branch protection.
howItWorks: Uses the issue as source of truth, or creates one after the plan passes; works only in a feature worktree.
Runs /ak:research or /ak:debug when needed, then `/ak:plan --tdd` with validate and red-team.
Implements via /ak:fix or /ak:cook --tdd --auto, updating issue labels along the way.
Loops /ak:code-review, then /ak:ship and `/ak:review-pr --fix --reply` until clean and CI is green.
--ship merges and fixes target CI (max 3 per blocker); ends with a Completion Report.
useWhen: Taking a GitHub issue to a reviewed, merge-ready PR in one command.
Turning a plain feature request into issue, plan, code, and PR.
Shipping beta then stable, each waiting for green CI (--both).
avoidWhen: Only planning: use /ak:plan or /ak:issue-to-plan.
Working on the current branch without issue or PR: use /ak:cook.
Vague product requirements: use /ak:brainstorm or /ak:advise first.

params.name: <github-issue-url | feature request>
params.desc: Issue URL or number from the current repo, or a plain request (issue created after plan gates).

params.name: --ship
params.desc: Merges after PR review and fixes target CI until green (max 3 fixes per blocker). Without it, stops at a reviewed PR.

params.name: --beta
params.desc: Ships to beta/dev via `/ak:ship beta`; default is stable via `/ak:ship official`. Overridden by --both.

params.name: --both
params.desc: Full beta stage through green CI, then stable. Implies --ship; red beta skips stable.

params.name: --advice
params.desc: kongming supervises every phase, stops on failed verify, and reviews the PR at green CI.

params.name: --ultra
params.desc: Best-of-5 mode for /ak:plan and /ak:code-review only. Much higher cost.

examples.note: Issue to reviewed PR labeled `ready to ship stable`, no merge.

examples.cmd: /ak:vibe --ship Add a date filter to the reports page
examples.note: Plain request: creates issue, plan, code, PR, merges, and waits for green CI.
Beta then stable, with kongming supervision and post-PR review.

tips: Vibe runs long; --ultra and --both multiply the cost.
`gh` needs rights for labels, issues, PRs, and merges, or the run stops.
CI failures from missing secrets or approvals are external blockers; tests are never weakened.
artifacts: plans/<timestamp>-<slug>/ TDD plan with validation and red-team

ak-bro.tagline: Restate the last assistant message in plain, short words.
ak-bro.summary: ak:bro rewrites the previous assistant message clearly and simply, keeping facts, warnings, and required actions. It adds no analysis, runs no tools, and replies in your language.
howItWorks: Uses only the immediately previous assistant message.
Replaces jargon with everyday words and briefly defines terms it must keep.
Cuts repetition, filler, and process narration; returns only the restatement.
With no previous message, asks you to paste text.
useWhen: The last answer was too long or jargon-heavy.
You need a short version of a report for a non-specialist.
You say "simplify that" or "say it plainly".
avoidWhen: Explaining a new topic: use /ak:explain.
Wanting new analysis or actions: bro adds nothing and runs no tools.
Making every answer simpler: use /ak:coding-level 0 or 1.

params.name: [last message]
params.desc: Source to restate; defaults to the previous assistant message.

examples.note: Right after a long technical answer, for a short plain version.
Restates the previous message in another requested language.

tips: Call it right after the answer you want simplified.
Warnings and uncertainty survive, so the short version is safe to act on.
Very cheap: no tools, no file reads.

ak-explain.tagline: Grounded explanations of concepts, code, systems, and errors.
ak-explain.summary: ak:explain builds an evidence-based mental model of a topic, code path, error, or document, separating facts from inference. --eli5 uses everyday analogies with warnings kept; --html makes an offline page with diagrams.
howItWorks: Takes the topic from the argument, open file, or conversation; asks one question if missing.
Reads actual source for repo paths and stack traces; never invents APIs or behavior.
Output: gist, core concepts, mechanism, example, caveats and failure modes.
--html uses ak:frontend-design and ak:diagram, falling back to inline SVG; fully offline and accessible.
Explaining errors is read-only; fixes go to a fix skill.
useWhen: Understanding a concept like JWT refresh tokens or the event loop.
Walking through a file or request flow with path citations.
Learning why an error happens before fixing it.
avoidWhen: Restating the last answer more simply: use /ak:bro.
Slides or visual diff review: use /ak:preview.
Fixing the error: use /ak:fix or /ak:debug.

params.name: [subject|path|URL]
params.desc: Topic, repo path, or URL; empty falls back to the open file or conversation.

params.name: --html
params.desc: Offline, accessible HTML saved to {plan_dir}/visuals/ or plans/visuals/explain-{slug}.html.

params.name: --eli5
params.desc: One everyday analogy mapped to the real system, terms defined, warnings and commands kept exactly.

examples.note: Default Markdown: gist, mental model, caveats.
Walkthrough of a specific file with citations, facts separated from inference.
Beginner-friendly analogy with warnings intact.

tips: Give a file path so the explanation follows real source.
--eli5 never softens dangerous warnings.
--html costs more tokens than Markdown.
